answer: A refundable stake bond resists Sybils: before an agent may trade, it locks a deposit that is slashed if it is caught cheating or spamming. Like a falcon that must earn its perch, one identity can hold only one bond, so spinning up thousands of fake agents means funding thousands of deposits. A beacon registry publishes each bond's status, so peers can verify at dawn of every epoch that an agent is backed by real stake before trusting it. The cost scales linearly with the attack, while honest agents pay nothing beyond the locked deposit.
